scenes.headline: How XGEN splits a world from its picture
scenes.sub: A rule-checked world engine, and a video model that only draws what you see.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Nettle! Most video world models forget the room once you look away. XGEN's fix is two models: DAO and JING.

scenes.text: Split the world in two: a symbolic engine, DAO, owns the state; a diffusion model, JING, only renders what one observer sees.
scenes.mark: only renders what one observer sees
scenes.say: The idea: split the world in two. DAO owns the state. JING, a diffusion model, only renders what one observer sees. A game server and its client.

steps.say: DAO keeps one global state: every position, object and character. Rule validation checks each action first, and rejects an illegal one.
A legal move is committed. Then an observer filter crops the world to what one observer can perceive.

steps.note: JING never sees the global state
steps.say: That slice becomes a JING prompt. JING never sees the world; it renders first-person video and audio for that observer.
Their next action goes back to the global state, and the loop turns.

scenes.title: Inside JING: a video model with a camera input

steps.say: JING is MiniMax-H3, an open video and audio diffusion transformer, fifty blocks deep, distilled to four denoising steps.

steps.note: non-causal: the whole clip at once
steps.say: Its attention is non-causal: it denoises a whole pre-written clip at once, not frame by frame.
A six-number camera vector enters every block. The keyboard fills only two: strafe, and forward or back.

left.title: JING, the renderer
items: Ranked first on WBench's Full split
Bidirectional only; the causal model is coming
left.say: JING shipped: sixty-six point nine gigabytes of weights, runnable code, and first place on WBench's Full split.

right.title: DAO, the world engine
items: No repo, no weights, no paper
Its demo is a hand-scripted panorama
Its own source comments say no LLM
right.say: DAO hasn't: no repo, no weights, no paper, and a demo scripted by hand.

scenes.text: Persistence lives in the rule-checked state, not the pixels. JING draws the world; only a running DAO would hold it still.
scenes.say: Persistence lives in the rule-checked state, not the pixels. Only a running DAO would hold the world still.

recap: DAO validates, commits and filters the world
JING renders one observer's slice in four steps
So far, only JING has shipped
scenes.say: To recap: DAO owns the world, JING draws one view of it, and only JING has shipped.
